correctness.rationale: The greedy matcher on a power of a permutation needs exactly 1+2d(V)+b(V) copies to embed VV, with d counting internal weak descents and b the closing weak descent. A weighted trace gives the square-root enumerator. The rank-one determinant identity and all-ones resolvent simplify the trace to the stated rational function. A cyclic-weak-descent lower bound plus per-letter parity proves the exact q-or-1 extremal classification. Independent direct position-subsequence sets matched 85 rational coefficients across 19 configurations, with 11992 additional criterion tests. Formal proof, not finite experiments, supports unbounded parameters.

value.rationale: The square-word count is a natural invariant of subsequence repetition; it measures distinct admissible repeated patterns, not the much more numerous positional embeddings. The closed bivariate generating function determines every length stratum of an infinite family simultaneously, and the sharp parity split classifies every longest square root for all q and k. The collapse from a transfer-matrix statistic to a short q-dependent rational formula plus the cyclic-descent rigidity has specific reusable structure and is not a finite table or an arbitrary parameter slice.
